title: Smoky split pea stew with purple sprouting broccoli

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is plain whole food or an allowed staple, such as tinned tomatoes, split peas and vegetable stock.

supermarket.reason: All the ingredients are everyday Tesco lines; purple sprouting broccoli is on the shelves in January at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a lidded casserole, a knife and a board, and the technique is simple simmering.

works.reason: 250g split peas with 500g parsnips, veg and 1.2 litres of stock makes a well-balanced stew for four, the simmer is judged by softness, and there is a splash-of-water safeguard.

honest_times.reason: Chopping an onion, carrots and garlic fits in 20 minutes because the parsnips are prepped during the simmer, and the steps add up to roughly the 60 minutes of cooking printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warming smoky stew suits mid-January, and 250g of purple sprouting broccoli steamed on top is a real share of the dish rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, homely British English with sensible cues such as 'until soft' and 'until just tender'.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling pulse and vegetable stew with plenty of protein and fibre that a family would happily eat again.
